subject: Quote Request
body:
Hi Clarissa,

Absolutely! I would be happy to provide any information you may need regarding our annual subscription license.

The annual subscription license allows for an unlimited number of projects and may be a more cost-effective option for you since our pricing schema is more efficient for large-scale research compared to smaller projects. Not only is it cheaper, but it also enables you and your colleagues to create projects whenever you like, without requiring a separate invoice for each one, as long as you stay within your quota.

The cost of the annual subscription licenses depends on the quota of the license. Our unit of measurement for the quota is called participant/week. Each participant/week, or P/W in short, represents the data that you can collect from 1 participant during 1 week. For example, 100 P/W means you collect data from 100 participants for 1 week. Now you can use this in any combination that you want. For example, instead of 100 participants for 1 week, you can conduct 2 studies but each with 50 participants and 1 week, as the total again would be 100 P/W. Another example, with 2,500 P/W you can do the following:
  • Collect data in 1 study, from 2,500 participants, each for 1 week.
  • Collect data in 5 studies, from 500 participants, each for 1 week.
  • Collect data in 5 studies, from 100 participants, each for 5 weeks.

Given all this information, here are a few suggestions for you:
  • Annual subscription license to collect survey responses from up to 2,500 P/W: CAD 2,908.00 (~ USD 2,093.22) per year.
  • Annual subscription license to collect survey responses from up to 5,000 P/W: CAD 3,208.00 (~ USD 2,309.16) per year.
  • Annual subscription license to collect survey responses from up to 10,000 P/W: CAD 3,808.00 (~ USD 2,741.05) per year.
As you can see, our pricing doesn't grow linearly and it's more efficient toward larger quotas than in smaller ones.

If you decide to proceed with this option, you can also include study IDs 3901 and 3902 within this license.

If you have any questions or would like to know the cost for any other P/W quota, please feel free to reach out.

Best,

Each participant/week, or P/W in short, represents the data that you can collect from 1 participant during 1 week. For example, 100 P/W means you collect data from 100 participants for 1 week. Now you can use this in any combination that you want. For example, instead of 100 participants for 1 week, you can conduct 2 studies but each with 50 participants and 1 week, as the total again would be 100 P/W.   • Collect data in 5 studies, from 500 participants, each for 1 week.
  • Collect data in 5 studies, from 100 participants, each for 5 weeks.
